a short-term (4-6 week) drought reduced the net ecosystem CO 2 uptake by 32% in the tropical rainforest mesoco- sm, with a major contribution to the reduction coming from the reduction of leaf area, and with the reduction in leaf area being a consequence of reduced leaf expansion and increased leaf shedding.
the functional diversity of photosynthesis in the rainforest mesocosms is the main reason for a rapid, large and persistent reduction of Aeco in response to a short drought.
the tropical forest mesocosm within Biosphere 2 is a valuable model system to study the functional response of rainforest to drought.

how tropical forests respond to climate variability, and how this response may change under future climatic conditions.
the eco- logical and evolutionary consequences of the functional diversity of photosynthesis and the mechanisms that allow tropical trees to cope with environmental stresses.
the mechan- isms of carbon and water exchange between the rainforest canopy and atmosphere and the effects of environmental change on these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tropical rainforest ecosystem studied here is very sensitive to water availability.
the functional diversity of the rainforest ecosystem, in terms of the diversity of responses to drought at the level of individuals, is the key to the maintenance of ecosystem function.
the tropical rainforest ecosystem is highly sensitive to drought, with a rapid and persistent decline of net carbon uptake rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tropical rainforest ecosystems have the capacity to cope with a 4- to 6-week drought, and that the response is reversible within weeks of rewatering.
the photosynthetic response of the tropical rainforest to drought is complex, and that the ecosystem response to drought is a combination of leaf-level physiological and morphological responses.

drought in a tropical rainforest ecosystem can be considered to be an acute disturbance, with a rapid and reversible response of ecosystem CO 2 exchange rate, and that the ecosystem response is a complex interplay of leaf area and leaf physiology, and the relative contributions of these components are species-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tropical forest trees are able to acclimate to the drought stress, and this is reflected in their ability to maintain high rates of net photosynthesis and high rates of carbon uptake.

the tropical rainforest mesoccosm is a useful model system for studying the responses to drought in a complex, multi- species ecosystem, and that the responses are complex and heterogeneous, even though the system is well controlled.
the rainforest ecosystem has a remarkable capacity to maintain its carbon balance during drought, but that this capacity is not limitless.
